Pay with your phone. Choose how to protect your savings.

Get early access on TestFlight

Wallet reads use Bitcoin peers and compact block filters. Keys are stored in this device’s Keychain; secret exports are explicit. No address-query service supplies the wallet’s balance.

Shared savings · choose the approval threshold

Share control with other people

Advanced · software signer tested; hardware integration unverified

Combine your phone with another signer

Use 2-of-2 MuSig2 so your phone and a separate key must both approve every payment. You can also use a MuSig2 group as one cosigner in a larger threshold vault.

Create a wallet and finish its backup

Create keys on the phone, write down the recovery phrase, and resume an unfinished backup after reopening the app.

Know before using it: A recovery phrase alone does not reconstruct this wallet’s historical scan. Keep the history-carrying backup too.

How we test: Create a wallet and finish its backup

  1. Create the wallet before network sync finishes.
  2. Complete the backup; reopen and reveal it only through the protected flow.

App scenarios: test01OnboardingCreateWallet, test09BackupResumeAndReveal . Inspect test runs and their results.

These tests drive the app against a disposable signet node. Images show test wallets; a screenshot or a test in the source is not a passing result. Check the run’s revision, failures, and result bundle.

Receive and recognize a payment

Show a fresh address and QR code. While Receive is open, peer-relayed payments appear as unconfirmed; confirmed payments enter the wallet’s history.

How we test: Receive and recognize a payment

  1. Mine a payment and find it through compact filters.
  2. Receive a normal transaction before mining it, then observe its confirmation in the app.

App scenarios: test02ReceiveAndFunding, test14IncomingPaymentBeforeConfirmation . Inspect test runs and their results.

Review, send, and follow confirmation

Choose a recipient and enter an amount. Review the full address, network fee, and total on the next screen, then send and follow confirmation.

How we test: Review, send, and follow confirmation

  1. Enter a recipient and amount without fee controls crowding the form.
  2. Edit a reviewed payment, then verify the new amount, full address, fee, and total before sending.
  3. Check that Bitcoin Core received the payment, open its diagnostics, and follow confirmation in the app.

Share control with other people

Choose a threshold such as 2 of 3: any two keys can approve a payment while one is unavailable. Start from Savings on the Wallet screen.

Know before using it: The threshold counts keys, not verified people. A 1-of-n policy allows one key to spend. Taproot hides the threshold until a script-path spend reveals it; key separation is not protection against every coercion scenario.

Read the advanced guide

How we test: Share control with other people

  1. Create shared savings from the Wallet screen and choose the co-owners and threshold.
  2. Fund the savings, review a request, and complete two approvals while the third signer stays absent.

Export and restore a wallet

Export a history-carrying bundle and verify it when importing. Secret-bearing exports require an explicit protected action.

Know before using it: Recovery is forward verification from the bundle’s saved history, not a historical rescan from twelve words.

How we test: Export and restore a wallet

  1. Export watch-only and secret-bearing bundles through their distinct controls.
  2. Import a funded bundle and check its verification report and wallet state.

App scenarios: test06ImportBundleVerification, test08ExportBundle . Inspect test runs and their results.

Keep everyday controls simple

Use Wallet, Send, People, and Settings without protocol controls crowding the normal flow. Turn on Advanced mode when those controls are useful.

How we test: Keep everyday controls simple

  1. Check the beginner navigation and hidden advanced controls.
  2. Turn Advanced mode on to reveal fee and peer controls, then hide them again.
